newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo to search for copper, zinc in Angola.
newsitem.headline: Anglo to search for copper, zinc in Angola.

text.p: South Africa's Anglo American Corporation has signed a contract with Angola to search for zinc and copper in its southwestern Namibe province, Angola's news agency Angop reported on Wednesday.
Anglo could not immediately confirm that the deal had been signed, but industry sources said the company had been negotiating the deal with Angola since 1992.
Angop said the contract involved a three-year prospecting licence, and the investment was worth over $1.2 million.
It said work would begin within two weeks.
Angop said the contract was signed on Tuesday between Anglo representative Roy Corrans and Director-General of Angola's Geology Institute, Germano de Araujo.
Araujo told reporters the government would not be a partner in the project and would not contribute financially to the prospecting phase.
The contract is one of the first to be signed by the Angolan government for the exploration of base metals since the country began its slow transition to peace in 1994 after two decades of civil war.
